source_title: New Coke: The Most Memorable Marketing Blunder Ever?
publisher_issuer: The Coca-Cola Company (official corporate history); corroborated by HISTORY.com and TIME
company_context: The Coca-Cola Company, losing cola-war share to Pepsi and seeing blind taste tests favor a sweeter formula, reformulated its flagship Coca-Cola for the first time in 99 years, launching 'New Coke' on April 23, 1985.
business_type: Carbonated soft-drink manufacturer (consumer packaged goods, beverages)
macro_context: Intense 'cola wars' with PepsiCo; Pepsi gaining on taste-test marketing; diet and non-cola beverages eroding share.
evidence_summary: Coca-Cola replaced its original formula with a sweeter 'New Coke' on April 23, 1985. Despite favorable blind taste tests, loyal customers revolted: the consumer hotline rose to ~1,500 calls/day (vs ~400 before), peaking around 8,000/day, with roughly 40,000 complaint letters. On July 11, 1985 the company reversed course and reintroduced the original formula as 'Coca-Cola Classic', 79 days after launch. The reversal restored sales and brand trust.

source_backed_metrics.consumer_calls_per_day_peak: approximately 8,000 (up from ~400 before the change; ~1,500/day by June)

owner_decision_context: Management, alarmed by Pepsi's taste-test-driven share gains, decided to change the flagship formula based on blind taste tests, underweighting the emotional brand attachment of loyal consumers.
action_taken: Reformulated and replaced original Coca-Cola with sweeter 'New Coke', discontinuing the original; then reversed the decision after 79 days by reintroducing the original formula as Coca-Cola Classic.
outcome_evidence: Surge in consumer complaints (calls rising from ~400 to ~8,000/day, ~40,000 letters) and public backlash forced reversal in 79 days; sales rebounded after Classic's return, confirming the action worsened standing before correction.

directly_stated: New Coke launched April 23, 1985; original returned as Coca-Cola Classic July 11, 1985 (79 days)
Consumer hotline calls rose from ~400/day to as many as ~8,000/day; ~40,000 complaint letters
The reformulation was reversed due to consumer backlash
inferred: The action damaged brand trust and short-term standing despite favorable taste tests (quality/trust failure driven by ignoring emotional brand equity)
The rapid reversal and sales rebound indicate the original decision was the proximate cause of distress
why_useful_for_opsiq: Outcome-10-then-9 case: a deliberate product action that ignored customer attachment, worsened standing, and was corrected. Tests whether the engine distinguishes a self-inflicted trust failure from a market-driven decline and credits the corrective reversal.
